title: 2019 Peach Bowl: LSU 63, Oklahoma 28 and Burrow's Record Half
question: What happened when Oklahoma played LSU in the 2019 Peach Bowl?
answer: No. 1 LSU beat No. 4 Oklahoma 63-28 in the Peach Bowl playoff semifinal on December 28, 2019, in Atlanta. Joe Burrow threw seven touchdown passes, all in the first half, as LSU led 49-14 at the break.
summary: LSU beat Oklahoma 63-28 in the Dec. 28, 2019 Peach Bowl playoff semifinal as Joe Burrow threw seven first-half TD passes and LSU outgained OU 692-322.
body: Oklahoma reached the College Football Playoff for a third straight season in 2019 with quarterback Jalen Hurts, the Heisman Trophy runner-up, leading a 12-1 team. The semifinal draw at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta was as tough as it gets: unbeaten, top-ranked LSU and Heisman winner Joe Burrow.

The game got away from the Sooners in a hurry. Burrow threw seven touchdown passes before halftime, tying the NCAA record for touchdown passes in a half and matching the mark for any college bowl game. LSU led 49-14 at the break. Justin Jefferson caught four of those scores, tying a bowl record, and finished with 14 catches for 227 yards.

Burrow added an eighth touchdown on a 2-yard run in the third quarter and finished 29 of 39 for 493 yards. LSU outgained Oklahoma 692 yards to 322 and moved on at 14-0 to the national championship game, while OU finished 12-2. The crowd of 78,347 set a Peach Bowl record.

The defeat was Oklahoma's third straight semifinal loss to an SEC opponent. When the Sooners finally won a New Year's Six game the next season, the AP noted that OU had allowed an average of 54 points across those three semifinals against Georgia, Alabama and LSU.
